use: A long low ancient caravan water trough carved from pale limestone. Thick rectangular sides with softly chipped corners, a dark shallow recessed interior, one rounded stone lip at the end. Sandy worn cream stone with ochre mineral staining and damp grey seams. No flowing water or surrounding paving, no modern tap or pipe. Roman eastern frontier utilitarian object, length approximately two metres.
